rules.name: ALLY OF THE BEASTS
rules.turn:
#acc ally-option : spirit e
ally-move S B From To, presence-of S P, at P From / ally-option S P
ally-move S B From To / ally-option S decline
move B To, beasts-at B From, land To, spirit:special S ally-of-the-beasts, has-presence S From
  ~ally-move S B From To
ally-move S B From To
  ?[rng] P
  !(ally-option S P)
  ~ally-choice S P To
ally-choice S C To, is C P, presence-of S P, ~move P To
rules.evidence: push fangs *171 l3 -> l2; ally-choice picks f1 (seeds 2,4) or f2 (seed 3): move f1 l2; or declines (seeds 7,1)
rules.notes: A trigger on the base `move` episode: `at`/`beasts-at` are read at the move's start, which is exactly 'moves from 1 of your lands'. First attempt read the destination after the move and got the old location; From/To must be passed along from the move itself. Two Beasts moving in parallel can both offer the same Presence (sibling concurrency).
rules.text: Your [Presence] may move with [Beasts] . (Whenever a [Beasts] moves from 1 of your lands to another land, you may move 1 [Presence] along with it.)

rules.name: CALL FORTH PREDATORS
rules.turn:
#acc predator-option : spirit e
call-forth S, presence-of S P, at P L, land L / predator-option S P
call-forth S / predator-option S decline
spirit-phase, spirit:special S call-forth-predators, ~call-forth S
call-forth S
  ?[rng] P
  !(predator-option S P)
  ~predator-choice S P
predator-choice S C, is C P, presence-of S P, at P L
  ~>move P out-of-game
  ~add-piece L beasts
rules.evidence: seeds 7,1: move f1 out-of-game; add-piece l3 beasts (new Beasts *7038 then pushed too)
rules.notes: 'Leaves the game' is a location distinct from `destroyed`, so effects that return destroyed Presence naturally cannot find it.
rules.text: During each Spirit Phase, you may replace 1 of your [Presence] with 1 [Beasts] . The replaced [Presence] leaves the game. (It was not destroyed, so things which return destroyed [Presence] cannot bring it back.)

language_issues: Reading a location 'after' a move from a sibling rule sees the pre-move value (the sibling is unordered with the moved fact); pass values from the triggering episode's arguments instead.
'You may' needs an explicit `decline` option row in the choice domain each time.
